pairs.question: Quid sit ius naturale?
pairs.answer: Ius naturale est, aut civile, aut gentium.
pairs.derivation: Chapter heading 'QVID SIT IVS NATVRALE' is a genuine interrogative posed and answered by Isidore. First-word capitalization kept; terminal '?' supplied. Answer is the opening sentence of the body; the bracketed editorial supplement '[est]' is stripped keeping the word 'est'. Window ends at the first full stop; what follows ('Ius naturale est commune omnium nationum...') elaborates with examples rather than giving the direct division.

pairs.question: Quid sit ius civile?
pairs.answer: Ius civile est quod quisque populus vel civitas sibi proprium humana divinaque causa constituit.
pairs.derivation: Heading 'QVID SIT IVS CIVILE' is an interrogative; the single-sentence body answers it. The chapter contains only this one sentence, so the whole body is the answer. Terminal '?' supplied on the question.

pairs.question: Quid sit ius gentium?
pairs.answer: Ius gentium est sedium occupatio, aedificatio, munitio, bella, captivitates, servitutes, postliminia, foedera pacis, indutiae, legatorum non violandorum religio, conubia inter alienigenas prohibita.
pairs.derivation: Heading 'QVID SIT IVS GENTIVM' answered by the opening definitional sentence. Window ends at the first full stop; what follows ('Et inde ius gentium, quia eo iure...') is an etymological aside, not the definition.

pairs.question: Quid sit ius militare?
pairs.answer: Ius militare est belli inferendi sollemnitas, foederis faciendi nexus, signo data egressio in hostem vel commissio.
pairs.derivation: Heading 'QVID SIT IVS MILITARE' answered by the opening definitional clause. Window ends at the first full stop; what follows ('Item signo dato receptio...') continues enumerating further items rather than giving the core definition.

pairs.question: Quid sit ius publicum?
pairs.answer: Ius publicum est in sacris et sacerdotibus, in magistratibus.
pairs.derivation: Heading 'QVID SIT IVS PVBLICVM' answered by the chapter's single sentence (the whole body). Terminal '?' supplied on the question.

pairs.question: Quid sit ius Quiritum?
pairs.answer: Ius Quiritum est proprie Romanorum, quo nulli tenentur nisi Quirites, id est Romani, tamquam de legitimis hereditatibus, de cretionibus, de tutelis, de usucapionibus.
pairs.derivation: Heading 'QVID SIT IVS QVIRITVM' answered by the opening definitional sentence. Window ends at the first full stop ('...de usucapionibus.'); what follows ('quae iura apud alium nullum populum reperiuntur...') is elaboration on the same.

pairs.question: Quid sit lex?
pairs.answer: Lex est constitutio populi, qua maiores natu simul cum plebibus aliquid sanxerunt.
pairs.derivation: Heading 'QVID SIT LEX' is an interrogative answered by the chapter's single defining sentence (the whole body). Terminal '?' supplied on the question.
